# Operations up to v3

Every operation that exists by `elbrus-v3` (the Elbrus 4C, the
baseline the GCC port targets), what it computes, how a compiler uses
it, and what is known about it. Operations only v1 (Elbrus-3M) had are
left out: no working machine exists. What v4 and v5 add is in
[operations-v5.md](operations-v5.md), v6 in
[operations-v6.md](operations-v6.md) and v7 in
[operations-v7.md](operations-v7.md). **Generated** by
`tools/isa-extract/gen_operations.py` from `operations-v3.yaml` (the
rules, hand-written), `binutils-ops.yaml`, the timing tables,
`lcc-usage.yaml` and the probes' assembly; edit the sources, not this
page.

Columns:

- **ISA**: the `elbrus-vN` versions that have it (8 is binutils'
  placeholder for future ones). Rows marked 1–2 don't exist on v3 and
  later (`v2ops.c`).
- **ALC**: the ALU channels it may issue in (blank: a control or
  syllable operation, bundle.md).
- **Does**: the result, with a, b, c the first to third source operand
  in gas order (stores: address, offset, data under `.ignore
  ld_st_style`). Lanes are numbered from the least significant.
  Results narrower than the register follow `setwd dbl`
  (registers.md). Details and corner cases are in the section named.
- **Lat**: scheduled latency in cycles to a consumer of the same kind
  (timing.md; "(v5)": measured on the Elbrus-8C2 only); several values
  for a row with several operations. Rows without a kernel of their
  own give timing.md's value for them, where it has one.
- **lcc v3 / v5**: how many times the operations of the row appear in
  the shared libraries of lcc 1.29.16's v3 and v5 sysroots
  (`lcc-usage.yaml`): what lcc relies on.
- **Run on hardware**: the probes (`tools/isa-probes`,
  `tools/abi/probes`) whose assembly executes the operations, and the
  machines (4C: Elbrus 4C, v3; 8C2: Elbrus-8C2, v5); "*n* of *m*" when
  not all of the row's operations ran. Rows without a probe were taken
  from the sources named in the row.

An operation's behaviour is checked when its probe compares results
with a model (semantics.c, semp.c, sem5.c, semx.c, semfx.c, semc.c,
fcomb.c, icomb.c, sqrt.c, getf.c, divx.c, stmqp.c) or records what
user mode gets (v2ops.c, ctlops.c: completes, or which signal); the
others use it in a larger test (loops, speculation, prefetch).

## Integer arithmetic and logic

One cycle in any channel unless noted. `s` forms are 32-bit, `d` forms 64-bit. The second operand may be a literal (bundle.md).

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `adds`, `addd` | 1–8 | 0–5 | a + b, wrapping. **Use:** `add<mode>3`. (semantics.md, "Integer arithmetic and logic") | 1 | 634k / 612k | aaurwct, abg, abi/callsstack_clash.s, abi/callsstack_tail.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `subs`, `subd` | 1–8 | 0–5 | a − b (`rsub` exists only as a combined stage). **Use:** `sub<mode>3`; `neg` is `subd 0, x`. | 1 | 66k / 59k | abi/callsstack_clash.s, abi/callsstack_tail.s, abi/debuginfo.s, abi/foldi55… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `ands`, `andd`, `ors`, `ord`, `xors`, `xord` | 1–8 | 0–5 | Bitwise and, or, xor. **Use:** `and`, `ior`, `xor<mode>3`; `xor x, -1` for `not`. | 1 | 26k / 24k | abi/callsstack_tail.s, abi/ctxsig.s, abi/dbl.s, abi/elfops/islocal.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `andns`, `andnd`, `orns`, `ornd`, `xorns`, `xornd` | 1–8 | 0–5 | a & ~b, a \| ~b, a ^ ~b (the **second** operand inverted). **Use:** Combine patterns for `(and (not b) a)` and friends. | 1 | 1.4k / 1.4k | abi/dbl.s, icomb, semantics, timeleft (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `muls`, `muld` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | Low 32 or 64 bits of the product (signed and unsigned alike). ALC0, 1, 3, 4; 4 cycles, 6 to an integer consumer. **Use:** `mul<mode>3`. | 4 | 21k / 18k | abi/dbl.s, abi/foldp129_greg, damwb, foldisa… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `smulx`, `umulx` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | 64-bit product of the two 32-bit operands, signed or unsigned. **Use:** `mulsidi3`, `umulsidi3` (lcc: `(long) a * b`). (semantics.md, "Other scalar operations") | 4 | 607 / 597 | pocchk4, semx, timeleft (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `smulhd`, `umulhd` | 3–8 | 0,1,3,4 | High 64 bits of the 128-bit product, signed or unsigned. **Use:** `smuldi3_highpart`, `umuldi3_highpart`, division by constants. | 4 | 1.0k / 1.0k | semantics (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `sdivs`, `sdivd`, `udivs`, `udivd` | 1–8 | 5 | Quotient truncated toward zero; division by zero is SIGFPE (`FPE_INTDIV`); `sdivd MIN, −1` = MIN. ALC5 only, shares the divider (timing.md, "Divider"); the result arrives on the FP side, so an integer op waits 2 more. **Use:** `div`, `udiv<mode>3`; `%` is divide, multiply, subtract (as lcc). Speculative (`,sm`) forms defer the fault. (semantics.md, "Division") | 11 (small quotients, up to 18); 13 to an integer op | 686 / 685 | abi/dbl.s, ctlleft, pmu2, pocchk… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `sdivx`, `udivx`, `smodx`, `umodx` | 1–8 | 5 | 64-bit a ÷ 32-bit b into 32 bits (quotient or remainder); SIGFPE for a zero divisor, a quotient that doesn't fit, and for the remainders when a shifted left by the divisor's leading zeros overflows. ALC5; `smodx` and `umodx` hold the divider 9 cycles. **Use:** Only for proven ranges. (semantics.md, "Other scalar operations") | 11 (`sdivx`, `udivx`), 10 (`smodx`, `umodx`); 13, 12 to an integer op | 3 / 3 | divx, semx, timeleft, timeleftv (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `sxt` | 1–8 | 0–5 | Extend b by mode a: 0, 1, 2 sign-extend 8, 16, 32 bits; 4, 5, 6 zero-extend them (3 = 2, 7 = 6). **Use:** `extend`, `zero_extend`; `sxt 6` is the free `x & 0xffffffff`. (semantics.md, "Integer arithmetic and logic") | 1 | 25k / 25k | abi/dbl.s, abi/hwscan.s, mas_be, pmu… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `merges`, `merged` | 1–8 | 0–5 | pred ? b : a: **a when the predicate is false**. **Use:** `mov<mode>cc`, conditional select. (semantics.md, "Integer arithmetic and logic") | 1 | 31k / 27k | abi/dbl.s, abi/glibcbuild_entry.s, foldi57_retpred, loops… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `popcnts`, `popcntd`, `lzcnts`, `lzcntd`, `bitrevs`, `bitrevd` | 2–8 | 0,1,3,4 | Number of set bits; leading zeros (width for 0); bit reversal. v2+. `popcnt`, `lzcnt` ALC1/4. **Use:** `popcount`, `clz` (`CLZ_DEFINED_VALUE_AT_ZERO` = width), `bitreverse`; `ctz` = `lzcnt (bitrev x)`. | 1 | 607 / 829 | abi/dbl.s, semantics, semp, timeleft (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `shls`, `shld`, `shrs`, `shrd`, `sars`, `sard`, `scls`, `scld`, `scrs`, `scrd` | 1–8 | 0–5 | Shift left, logical right, arithmetic right, rotate left, rotate right; the count is b modulo the width. **Use:** `ashl`, `lshr`, `ashr`, `rotl`, `rotr<mode>3`; `SHIFT_COUNT_TRUNCATED` holds. (semantics.md, "Shifts and rotates") | 1 | 62k / 59k | abi/dbl.s, abi/elfops/islocal.s, abi/foldi55, abi/kernleft.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `getfs`, `getfd` | 1–8 | 0–5 | Field extract: rotate a right by b's offset, keep *len* bits, zero- or sign-extend (v1–v4 take the sign bit from b's BYTE field, v5 from the field's top; operations-v5.md). **Use:** `extzv`, `extv`, shift-and-mask, sign-extending shift pairs, wide low masks. (semantics.md, "Field extract") | 1 | 15k / 13k | abi/dbl.s, foldisa, getf, icomb… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `insfs`, `insfd` | 1–7 | 0,1,3,4 | Rotate a right by b's offset, then replace its low *len* bits by c's. ALC0, 1, 3, 4. **Use:** `insv` with a rotate back (`scl`), as lcc stores bit-fields. (semantics.md, "Other scalar operations") | 1 | 13k / 12k | apb-loop, pmu2, pocchk2, pocchk6… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `mpsadbh` | 3–8 | 1,4 | Four 16-bit sums of absolute byte differences, lane i = Σ \|a.byte[i+j] − b.byte[j]\| (x86 `mpsadbw` on 64 bits). v3+. (semantics.md, "Other scalar operations") | 2 |  | semx (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

## Integer compares

Into a predicate (`%predN`), from a − b (or a & b) tested like x86 flags. Compare → predicated operation 2 cycles, → `ct` 3.

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cmposb`, `cmpodb`, `cmpbsb`, `cmpbdb`, `cmpesb`, `cmpedb`, … (16 operations) | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | o: signed overflow of a − b; b: a < b unsigned; e: a = b; be: a ≤ b unsigned; s: a − b negative; p: even parity of its low byte; l: a < b signed; le: a ≤ b signed. No ne/gt/ge forms: swap operands or negate at the use. **Use:** `cbranch`, `cstore`, `mov<mode>cc` conditions; ALC0, 1, 3, 4. (semantics.md, "Integer compares") | 2; 3 to `ct` | 194k / 183k | aaurwct, abi/callsstack_clash.s, abi/callsstack_tail.s, abi/ctpr.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `cmpandesb`, `cmpandedb`, `cmpandssb`, `cmpandsdb`, `cmpandpsb`, `cmpandpdb`, `cmpandlesb`, `cmpandledb` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | The same tests on a & b: e zero, s sign bit, p even parity of the low byte, le ≤ 0 signed. **Use:** Bit tests (`if (x & m)`); lcc tests FP compare flags with them. (semantics.md, "Integer compares") | 2; 3 to `ct` | 14k / 13k | ctlleft, loops, p28, pocchk5… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `cctopo`, `cctopb`, `cctope`, `cctopbe`, `cctops`, `cctopp`, `cctopl`, `cctople` | 1–8 | 0,3 | Predicate: x86 condition c on b's low 32 bits read as EFLAGS (`o` OF, `b` CF, `e` ZF, `be` CF\|ZF, `s` SF, `p` PF, `l` SF≠OF, `le` ZF\|(SF≠OF)). ALC0/3; 2 cycles to a predicated op. **Use:** With the flag forms below, e.g. overflow checks. (semantics.md, "x86 flag operations") | 2; 3 to `ct` |  | pocchk4, pocchk5, semx (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

## x86 flag operations

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `adds_fb`, `adds_fh`, `adds_fw`, `subs_fb`, `subs_fh`, `subs_fw`, … (66 operations) | 1–8 | 0,3 | Return the x86 EFLAGS the operation would set (CF 0x01, PF 0x04, AF 0x10, ZF 0x40, SF 0x80, OF 0x800) as a 32-bit result, for operand width b/h/w/d: add, sub, the logic operations, inc/dec (a ± b, CF from c), shifts and rotates (old flags in c), 32 × 32 multiplies. For x86 binary translation; ALC0/3; a 32-bit result (dbl applies). **Use:** `adds_fw` + `cctopo` give `__builtin_add_overflow`'s flag (lcc doesn't use them). (semantics.md, "x86 flag operations") | 2 to an integer op or `cctop` in its cluster, 4 to the other; store data 1 (3 across); `[su]mulx_f*` 6 (4 to an FP-side op) |  | damwb, pocchk4, pocchk5, semx… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

## Combined integer operations

`X_Y a, b, c` = Y(c, X(a, b)): two ordinary operations chained in ALC1 or ALC4 with the latency of both (2; 4 to the other cluster). They save an instruction slot, not time (semantics.md, "FP min, max and combined operations").

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `and_ands`, `and_andd`, `andn_ands`, `andn_andd`, `or_ands`, `or_andd`, … (252 operations) | 1–7 | 1,4 | Y(c, X(a, b)), `rsub` being t − c. Every one equals the two ordinary operations (icomb.c, 252 of v3's). **Use:** Peephole fusion of dependent pairs where channels are short; lcc rarely uses them. (semantics.md, "FP min, max and combined operations") | 2 | 9.6k / 8.6k | icomb, pocchk, pocchk4, timeleft (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `merge_ands`, `merge_andd`, `merge_andns`, `merge_andnd`, `merge_ors`, `merge_ord`, … (18 operations) | 1–7 | 1,4 | Y(c, merge(a, b, pred)): select, then the second stage. **Use:** Adding, subtracting or or-ing a select into a value; with arms 0 and 1 a condition held in a predicate (a 0/1 `cstore` combined into its user): `merge_addd 0, 1, x, dst, pred` = x + (pred ? 1 : 0), `merge_subd` x − pred, `merge_ord` x \| pred. lcc uses them in unrolled and pipelined loops: carry and borrow chains (`mpn_add`: `cmpbdb`, then `merge_addd 0, 1` of the carry; `__quadmath_mpn_*`, `__divtf3`, glibc's `round_and_return`), counts (`n += a[i] < k`) and select-and-accumulate (a sum of absolute byte differences: `merge_adds` of `a − b` and `b − a` into the sum under `cmpssb`'s predicate). In straight-line code it keeps `merged` + `addd`, and `(c ? a : b) + d` becomes two predicated `addd`. 115 uses in its v3 libraries, 97 of them with arms `0x0, 0x1`. (semantics.md, "Other scalar operations") | 2 | 115 / 102 | semx (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

## Floating point

IEEE single and double in the general registers, `%pfpfr` holding the rounding mode and flags (x86 MXCSR layout); 4 cycles in ALC0, 1, 3, 4 (v5 also 2, 5). Operations set the denormal flag for a denormal operand. `s` forms keep the upper half of their destination.

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fadds`, `faddd`, `fsubs`, `fsubd`, `fmuls`, `fmuld` | 1–8 | 0–5 | a + b, a − b, a × b, correctly rounded. **Use:** `add`, `sub`, `mul<mode>3`. | 4 | 10k / 10k | abi/dbl.s, apbleft, damwb, foldisa… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `fdivs`, `fdivd` | 1–8 | 5 | a ÷ b, correctly rounded, IEEE flags. ALC5 (divider), 11 / 14 cycles, 13 / 16 to an integer op. **Use:** `div<mode>3`. (semantics.md, "Square root and reciprocals") | 11, 14 | 791 / 789 | fpcost, fpenv, pmu2, pocchk2… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `fsqrts`, `fsqrtid`, `fsqrttd` | 1–8 | 5 | `fsqrts` √a; a double square root is `fsqrtid a, t` then `fsqrttd a, t, r`, correctly rounded as a pair (`fsqrtid` alone is an intermediate in its own format). ALC5. **Use:** `sqrt<mode>2` (keep the pair together). (semantics.md, "Square root and reciprocals") | 12 (`fsqrts`); 11 + 14 (`fsqrtid`, `fsqrttd`); 14, 13, 16 to an integer op | 155 / 155 | fpenv, pmu2, pocchk5, sqrt… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `frcps`, `frsqrts` | 1–8 | 5 | 12-bit estimates of 1/a and 1/√a, no flags. **Use:** `-ffast-math` reciprocal estimates with Newton steps (lcc never). (semantics.md, "Square root and reciprocals") | 6; 8 to an integer op |  | sqrt (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `fmaxs`, `fmaxd`, `fmins`, `fmind` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | x86 `maxsd`/`minsd`, **b** if either is a NaN or both are zeros. 2 cycles, 4 to an integer op. **Use:** `smax`, `smin` only under `-ffinite-math-only` (and no signed zeros), or for `a > b ? a : b` and `a < b ? a : b`; not for `>=` or `<=`, which lcc `-O3` maps to them too, wrongly for signed zeros. (semantics.md, "FP min, max and combined operations") | 2 | 39 / 39 | fpenv, semantics, semx (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `fcmpeqsb`, `fcmpeqdb`, `fcmpltsb`, `fcmpltdb`, `fcmplesb`, `fcmpledb`, … (16 operations) | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | Predicate: a c b, quiet for eq, neq, uod, od, signalling for lt, le, nlt, nle; neq, nlt, nle are true when unordered. 4 cycles to a predicated op, 5 to `ct`. **Use:** `cbranch`, `cstore` for FP; swap operands for gt/ge. (semantics.md, "Floating-point compares") | 4; 5 to `ct` | 3.1k / 2.8k | foldi57_retpred, native, pmu2, semantics… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `fcmpeqs`, `fcmpeqd`, `fcmplts`, `fcmpltd`, `fcmples`, `fcmpled`, … (16 operations) | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | All ones (64 bits, or the low 32 for `s`) if a c b, else 0: x86 `cmpsd`/`cmpss`. **Use:** Branch-free FP selects with `and`/`andn`. (semantics.md, "Floating-point compares") | 2 |  | fpenv, pocchk5, semx (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `fcmpudsf`, `fcmpuddf`, `fcmpodsf`, `fcmpoddf` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | x86 `ucomisd`/`comisd` flags into a register: less 0x01, equal 0x40, greater 0, unordered 0x45; `ud` quiet, `od` signalling. **Use:** C's `isless` family: `fcmpuddf`, then an integer test of the flags (lcc: `cmpesb r, 1` for `isless`, two `cmpesb` and `landp` for `islessequal`); pipelined like any FP operation (lcc's `c += isless (a[i], b[i])` is a one-instruction kernel on v5). (semantics.md, "Floating-point compares") | 4 to an integer op or `cctop`, in either cluster | 160 / 161 | native, pocchk5, semantics (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `fstois`, `fstoistr`, `fstoid`, `fstoidtr`, `fdtois`, `fdtoistr`, `fdtoid`, `fdtoidtr` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | FP → integer: single or double to 32 or 64 bits, in the current rounding mode or truncated (`tr`); out of range or NaN gives the integer indefinite (0x80…0) and invalid. 4 cycles to a consumer of their format, 6 to an integer op. **Use:** `fix_trunc`, `lrint<mode><mode>2`. (semantics.md, "Other scalar operations") | 4; 6 to an integer op | 238 / 260 | abi/dbl.s, fpenv, semx, tagx (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `istofs`, `istofd`, `idtofs`, `idtofd` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | 32- or 64-bit signed integer → single or double, current rounding mode. **Use:** `float<mode><mode>2`; unsigned via a fix-up sequence. (semantics.md, "Other scalar operations") | 4; 6 to an integer op | 816 / 832 | fpenv, semx (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `fstofd`, `fdtofs` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | Single → double (exact), double → single (rounded). **Use:** `extendsfdf2`, `truncdfsf2`. (timing.md, "Formats") | 4; 6 to an integer op | 425 / 425 | fpenv, semx, timeleftv (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `fdtoifd`, `fstoifs` | 3–8 | 0,1,3,4 | Round b to an integral value with a as x86 `roundsd`'s immediate (bits 0–1 mode, bit 2 use `%pfpfr`, bit 3 no inexact). v3+. **Use:** `floor`, `ceil`, `btrunc`, `roundeven<mode>2` with a = 9, 0xa, 0xb, 8 (no inexact, as C23 and GCC's default for C require); `nearbyint` 0xc, `rint` 4. lcc and MCST's libm use 1, 2, 3 for floor, ceil and trunc, which raise inexact. C `round` has no mode (lcc: x + copysign (0.5, x), truncated, with range guards). (semantics.md, "Other scalar operations"; every immediate checked by pocchk5.c) | 4 | 146 / 152 | pocchk5, semx (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

## Combined FP operations

`X_Y a, b, c` = Y(c, X(a, b)) with a rounding after each stage, 8 cycles; the packed forms work lane by lane with `hadd`, `hsub` and `addsub` stages (semantics.md, "FP min, max and combined operations").

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fmul_adds`, `fmul_addd`, `fmul_subs`, `fmul_subd`, `fadd_adds`, `fadd_addd`, … (18 operations) | 1–7 | 0–5 | (a X b) then Y with c as the first operand: `fmul_addd` = a × b + c, `fmul_subd` = c − a × b, `fmul_rsubd` = a × b − c; **two roundings**. **Use:** Multiply-add only under `-ffp-contract=fast`, never for `fma()`; lcc uses `fmul_add*` in loops. | 8 | 540 / 667 | fcomb, fpenv, pmu2, pocchk2… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pfmul_adds`, `pfmul_addd`, `pfmul_subs`, `pfmul_subd`, `pfadd_adds`, `pfadd_addd`, … (45 operations) | 1–7 | 0–5 | The same on 64-bit packed singles (and `d` scalar doubles), with hadd(x, y) = (x0 + x1, y0 + y1), hsub likewise, addsub(x, y) = (x0 − y0, x1 + y1). | 8 |  | fcomb (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

## 80-bit (x87 extended) operations

`long double`: a 64-bit significand in the register and sign and exponent in its 16-bit extended part, under `%fpcr`/`%fpsr` (x87 control and status words). Every operation equals x87 code exactly, including rounding first to the precision control and then to a narrower result (semantics.md, "80-bit operations").

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fxaddss`, `fxadddd`, `fxaddsx`, `fxadddx`, `fxaddxx`, `fxaddxd`, … (25 operations) | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | a (80-bit) op b (type of the first suffix letter: single, double, 80-bit) → result of the second letter's type; `rsub` is b − a. **Use:** `long double` arithmetic, also with a narrower operand or result. | 5 (`fxmul` with an 80-bit result 4); 7 to an integer op (6); 8C2: 7 from an FP result into the single or double b | 5.0k / 5.0k | semfx, timeleft (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `fxdivss`, `fxdivdd`, `fxdivsx`, `fxdivdx`, `fxdivxx`, `fxdivxd`, `fxdivxs` | 1–8 | 5 | a ÷ b as above, ALC5. **Use:** `divxf3` `fxdivxx`. lcc uses a float or double divisor as it is (`a / d` = `fxdivdx a, d`; a constant exact as a single goes in as a 32-bit literal, `a / 3.0L` = `fxdivsx a, 0x40400000`, and `a / 4.0L` stays a division), rounds a narrower quotient in the same operation, as x87 `fdiv` then a narrow `fstp` (`(double) (a / b)` `fxdivxd`, `(float) (a / b)` `fxdivxs`, `(double) (a / d)` `fxdivdd`), and converts an integer divisor first (`istofx`). A float or double dividend takes `fxdivt*`. | 16; 18 to an integer op; 8C2: 18 into the single or double b | 368 / 367 | semfx, timeleft, timeleftv (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `fxdivtss`, `fxdivtsx`, `fxdivtdd`, `fxdivtdx` | 1–8 | 5 | src1 ÷ src2 with src1 a single (`s`) or double (`d`) and src2 80-bit; the result as the second letter. x87 `fld src1; fld src2; fdivrp; fstp` exactly, rounded to the precision control, then to a single or double result; ALC5. **Use:** `divxf3` with a single or double dividend. lcc: `float` or `double` ÷ `long double` (`fxdivtsx`, `fxdivtdx`), the same narrowed back (`fxdivtss`, `fxdivtdd`), and constants exact as a single (`1.0L / x`: `adds 0, 0x3f800000` puts the single in a register, as src1 takes no long literal, then `fxdivtsx`; `0.1L / x` is an 80-bit constant and `fxdivxx`). (semantics.md, "80-bit operations") | 16; 18 to an integer op; 8C2: 18 into the single or double src1 | 20 / 20 | sregs (4C, 8C2, 2C3); semfx ran them with the operands swapped |

## Packed integer (64-bit registers)

Lanes of 8 (b), 16 (h), 32 (w) or 64 (d) bits, little-endian. Mostly 1 cycle (multiplies, SAD and `phminposuh` 2) to packed or FP consumers, 4 to integer ones; add/sub/compare/min/max/average forms in ALC0/3, multiplies, `pmadd*`, `psadbw`, unpacks and packs in ALC1/4 (v3). Semantics follow the community qemu's `helper_vec.c` except the points in semantics.md, "Packed operations of v3".

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `paddb`, `paddh`, `paddw`, `paddd`, `psubb`, `psubh`, `psubw`, `psubd` | 1–8 | 0,3 | Lane-wise add or subtract, wrapping. **Use:** `add`/`sub` on `V8QI`, `V4HI`, `V2SI`. | 1 | 374 / 493 | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `paddsb`, `paddsh`, `paddusb`, `paddush`, `psubsb`, `psubsh`, `psubusb`, `psubush` | 1–8 | 0,3 | Lane-wise saturating, signed or unsigned (x86 `paddsb` …). **Use:** `ssadd`, `usadd`, `sssub`, `ussub`. | 1 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pmaxsb`, `pmaxsh`, `pmaxsw`, `pmaxub`, `pmaxuh`, `pmaxuw`, `pminsb`, `pminsh`, `pminsw`, `pminub`, `pminuh`, `pminuw` | 1–8 | 0,3 | Lane-wise maximum, minimum, signed or unsigned. **Use:** `smax`, `umax`, `smin`, `umin`. | 1 | 153 / 51 | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pavgusb`, `pavgush` | 1–8 | 0,3 | Lane-wise (a + b + 1) >> 1 unsigned (x86 `pavgb`, `pavgw`). **Use:** `uavg<mode>3_ceil`. | 1 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pcmpeqb`, `pcmpeqh`, `pcmpeqw`, `pcmpeqd`, `pcmpgtb`, `pcmpgth`, `pcmpgtw`, `pcmpgtd` | 1–8 | 0,3 | All-ones lanes where a = b, or a > b signed. **Use:** `vec_cmp`, masks for `pmerge`. | 1 | 453 / 80 | semp, tagx (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pmullh`, `pmulhh`, `pmulhuh`, `pmulhrsh` | 1–8 | 1,4 | 16-bit lanes: low half of the product, high half signed or unsigned, (a × b + 0x4000) >> 15 (x86 `pmulhrsw`). **Use:** `mul`, `smulhs`, `umulhs`, `smulhrs` on `V4HI`. | 2 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pmaddh`, `pmaddubsh` | 1–8 | 1,4 | `pmaddh`: x86 `pmaddwd`; `pmaddubsh`: signed bytes of **a** × unsigned bytes of **b**, pairs summed with signed saturation (x86 `pmaddubsw` with the roles swapped). **Use:** Dot products (`sdot_prod`). | 2 | 222 / 231 | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pmulubhh` | 2–8 | 1,4 | 16-bit lanes: (unsigned byte i of a × signed halfword i of b + 0x80) >> 8, bytes 0–3 of a. | 2 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `psadbw` | 1–8 | 1,4 | Sum of the 8 absolute byte differences in the low bits (x86 `psadbw`). **Use:** `usad`, `sad` reductions. | 2 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `psignb`, `psignh`, `psignw` | 3–8 | 0,3 | x86 `psign`: lane of a negated, kept or zeroed by the sign of b's lane. **Use:** `abs<mode>2` on `V8QI`, `V4HI`, `V2SI` as `psign* a, a` (doc/gcc-port-plan.md, P32; the most negative value stays as it is, as `abs` wraps); x86 `psign` (lcc's `_mm_sign_epi8` is two `psignb`). lcc's own loops compute `abs` with `psrah`, `xord`, `psubh`. | 1 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

| `psllqh`, `psllql`, `psrlqh`, `psrlql` | 1–8 | 1,4 | Shift a:b (a high) as one 128-bit value by 8 × imm bits, keep the low (`l`) or high (`h`) half; 16 and more give 0. **Use:** Byte-granular vector shifts and alignment. (semantics.md, "Packed operations of v3") | 1 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `packsshb`, `packushb`, `packsswh`, `packuswh` | 1–8 | 1,4 | Narrow with signed or unsigned saturation: halfwords → bytes, words → halfwords; **a's lanes go to the high half**, b's to the low half. **Use:** `vec_pack_ssat`, `vec_pack_usat` (swap the operands). | 1 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

| `pshufb` | 2–7 | 0,1,3,4 | Byte i from mask c's byte: bit 7 set gives a constant (bits 5–6: 0, 0x7f, 0x80, 0xff), else bits 0–2 pick a byte of a (bit 3 set) or b; v5 adds invert, bit-reverse and sign-replicate in bits 4–6, **v3 ignores them**. **Use:** `vec_perm` on 64 bits, byte swaps (`bswap` when MAS bit 3 can't be used). (semantics.md, "Packed operations of v3") | 1 | 1.0k / 666 | mas_be, semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pshufh`, `pshufw` | 1–8 | 1,4 | `pshufh a, imm`: halfword i = a's halfword (imm >> 2i) & 3 (x86 `pshufw`); `pshufw a, b, imm`: word i from a (selector > 1) or b, word selector bit 0. **Use:** `vec_perm` with constant selectors. | 1 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

| `pextrh`, `pinsh` | 1–8 | 1,4 | `pextrh a, b, imm`: halfword imm of a:b (0–3 from b), imm > 7 differs by machine; `pinsh a, b, imm`: a with halfword imm & 3 replaced by b's low halfword. **Use:** `vec_extract`, `vec_set`. (semantics.md, "Packed operations of v3") | 1 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pmovmskb`, `pmovmskps`, `pmovmskpd` | 1–8 | 1,4 | Sign bits gathered: `pmovmskb` b's 8 bytes in bits 0–7, a's in 8–15; `ps` 2 + 2 words; `pd` 1 + 1 doubles. **Use:** `vec_pack_sfix`-free mask tests, `memchr`-style loops. | 1 | 31 / 0 | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

| `phaddh`, `phaddw`, `phaddsh`, `phsubh`, `phsubw`, `phsubsh` | 3–8 | 0,3 | Horizontal add or subtract of adjacent pairs (saturating `s`), a's pairs into the low half, b's into the high half (x86 `phaddw` …). **Use:** Reductions. | 1 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pandd`, `pandnd`, `pord`, `pxord` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | 64-bit bitwise and, a & ~b, or, xor, on the packed side (latency 1 to packed and FP consumers). **Use:** Logic between packed values without the FP → integer crossing. | 1 | 58 / 129 | foldisa, semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

## Packed FP (64-bit registers)

`pf*s` treat the register as two singles, `pf*d` as one double (identical to the scalar operation, kept for encoding symmetry); `pfdivs`, `pfsqrts` and the conversions other than `pfstoifs` work on one lane (semantics.md, "Packed operations of v3"). 4 cycles (min, max and compares 2), 6 to an integer op; flags as the scalar operations (semantics.md, "Packed operations of v3").

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pfadds`, `pfaddd`, `pfsubs`, `pfsubd`, `pfmuls`, `pfmuld`, `pfmaxs`, `pfmaxd`, `pfmins`, `pfmind` | 1–8 | 0–5 | Lane-wise add, subtract, multiply, x86-style max and min. **Use:** `V2SF` arithmetic. | 2, 4 |  | fpcost, fpenv, semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pfdivs`, `pfdivd`, `pfsqrts`, `pfsqrttd` | 1–8 | 5 | `pfdivs`, `pfdivd`: IEEE values but **no flags**; `pfdivs` divides the low singles only (not packed, as `pfsqrts` = `fsqrts` of the low single); `pfsqrttd` = `fsqrttd`. From v5 `pfdivd` and `pfsqrttd` take 2 cycles more than `fdivd` and `fsqrttd`. **Use:** Only where IEEE flags don't matter (`-fno-trapping-math`), one lane at a time. lcc divides a `V2SF` GNU vector with `getfd` (the high singles), two `pfdivs` and `insfd`, even without `-ffast-math`; its loops use scalar `fdivs`, `fdivd`, `fsqrts` and `fsqrtid` + `fsqrttd`, also under `-ffast`. (semantics.md, "Packed operations of v3") | 11 (`pfdivs`), 12 (`pfsqrts`), 14 (`pfdivd`, `pfsqrttd`; 16 on v5 and v6) |  | semp, sqrt, timeleft, timeleftv (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pfcmpeqs`, `pfcmpeqd`, `pfcmplts`, `pfcmpltd`, `pfcmples`, `pfcmpled`, … (16 operations) | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | All-ones lanes where the compare holds; eq, neq, od, uod quiet (also on qemu's error list), lt/le signal. **Use:** `vec_cmpv2sfv2si` and `vcond_mask` with `pmerge y, x, mask`: lt, le, eq directly, gt, ge with the operands swapped, `!(a < b)` by swapping the select's arms, `!=` `pfcmpneqs`, unordered `pfcmpuods`. lcc's v3 vectorizer uses `pfcmplts`, `pfcmples`, `pfcmpeqs` + `pmerge` for masks and counts (`n += a[i] < k`, with `paddw`) at `-O3`, and for selects only under `-faligned` (or `-ffast`); it keeps `!=`, unordered and `isless` loops scalar. GNU vector `!=` is `pfcmpneqs`, and its `_mm_cmpnlt_ps`, `_mm_cmpunord_ps`, `_mm_cmpord_ps` are `pfcmpnlts`, `pfcmpuods`, `pfcmpods`. lt, le, nlt, nle signal on quiet NaNs, so a quiet relational vector compare (`isless`) is no single packed operation. The `d` forms are one double, as `fcmp*d`. | 2 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pfhadds`, `pfhsubs`, `pfaddsubs` | 3–8 | 0–5 | Horizontal add/subtract (a's pair low, b's high); `pfaddsubs` (a0 − b0, a1 + b1). | 4 |  | semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pfdtofs`, `pfdtois`, `pfdtoistr`, `pfstofd`, `pfdtoifd`, `pfstoifs` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | One lane, as the scalar operation of the same name (`pfdtofs` = `fdtofs`, …): `pfdtofs`, `pfdtois`, `pfdtoistr` write one 32-bit result, `pfstofd` reads the low single, `pfdtoifd` rounds one double; only `pfstoifs` is packed, rounding both singles to integral with mode a. **Use:** `pfstoifs`: `floor`, `ceil`, `btrunc`, `roundeven`, `rint`, `nearbyint` on `V2SF` with a = 9, 0xa, 0xb, 8, 4, 0xc, as for scalar `fstoifs` (both lanes checked with every immediate in pocchk5.c); lcc gives scalar `fstoifs` 1, 2, 3, which raise inexact, its `_mm_floor_ps` on v3 is two `pfstoifs 0x1`, and its vectorizer keeps these loops scalar. The rest convert one lane at a time: lcc's `__builtin_convertvector` from `V2SF` to `V2DF` is `getfd` (the high single) and two `pfstofd`, from `V2DF` to `V2SF` or `V2SI` two `pfdtofs` or `pfdtoistr` joined by `insfd`; it never uses `pfdtois` or `pfdtoifd` (its x86 headers emit `fdtois`, `fdtoifd`). | 4 |  | pocchk5, semp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

## Memory

Address a + b (64-bit), MAS in the operation's `mas=` field (bit 3 byte swap, bits 5–6 cache hints, mod in bits 0–2: speculation and atomics). Loads take 3 cycles from L1 and zero-extend; stores take their data without the FP-side or cluster penalty. Up to four loads (ALC0, 2, 3, 5) and two stores (ALC2, 5) a cycle.

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ldb`, `ldh`, `ldw`, `ldd` | 1–8 | 0,2,3,5 | Load 1, 2, 4, 8 bytes, zero-extended. `,sm` is speculative (diagnostic value instead of a fault). **Use:** `mov<mode>` loads; `zero_extend` from memory is free. (speculation.md; semantics.md, "Byte-swapped memory accesses") | 3, 5 (v6) | 331k / 326k | abg, abi/callsstack_tail.s, abi/ctpr.s, abi/ctxsig.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `stb`, `sth`, `stw`, `std` | 1–8 | 2,5 | Store the low 1, 2, 4, 8 bytes of the data. ALC2/5. **Use:** `mov<mode>` stores. |  | 139k / 124k | aaurwct, abg, abi/callsstack_clash.s, abi/callsstack_tail.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `ldaab`, `ldaah`, `ldaaw`, `ldaad`, `ldaaq`, `staab`, `staah`, `staaw`, `staad`, `staaq` | 1–8 | 2,5 | Array access through an AAU descriptor `%aadN` and index `%aastiN` (+ literal); `incr` advances the index by `%aaincrN` × the element size. Stores obey loop-mode store suppression; neither loads nor stores need alignment (on v3 too). A MAS acts as on `ld`/`st` (cache hints, `be`); mod 2 and 3 make an AAU load an ordinary load, not a DAM check. **AAU loads are served from L2**: 9 cycles to an integer op on the 4C, 11 on the 8C2, 13 on the 2C3, in either cluster, and they fill no L1 line. **Use:** Pipelined loops: lcc's APB loops and its `#pragma vector nontemporal` loops (`mas=0x60`) store with `staa`; lcc emits no `ldaa`. (apb.md, "AAU stores", "AAU loads"; loops.md) |  | 1.0k / 781 | apb, apbleft, apbst, loops… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `ldcsb`, `ldcsh`, `ldcsw`, `ldcsd`, `ldcsq`, `lddsb`, … (60 operations) | 1–8 | 0,2,3,5 | Loads and stores through x86-style segment registers set up by a binary translator; **fault in user mode** (SIGILL, SIGSEGV or SIGBUS). (semantics.md, "Memory, tag and descriptor operations") |  |  | semc (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `ldgdb`, `ldgdh`, `ldgdw`, `ldgdd`, `ldgdq`, `stgdb`, … (15 operations) | 1–8 | 0,2,3,5 | Loads/stores relative to the global (GD) or compilation-unit (CUD) descriptor; SIGSEGV `SEGV_BNDERR` in an ordinary 64-bit process, but lcc's 32-bit code (`-mptr32`) makes every memory access with `ldgd*`/`stgd*`: the two 32-bit operands are summed modulo 2³², and past `0xf000_0000` they are `SEGV_BNDERR` (x86-support.md; spec/abi/mode32.md); lcc's protected code (`-mptr128`) reads globals with them, checked against the module's `GD` (spec/abi/protected-mode.md). In a protected process `ldcud*` read the module's own code, `SEGV_BNDERR` past `CUD`'s size; lcc never emits them (protected-mode.md, "Operations"). | `ldgd*` 3 (v6 5), as the `ld*` of its width; `stgd*` as `st*` (32-bit processes; `ldcud*` not measured) |  | abi/mode32/lat32, abi/mode32/mode32.s, semc (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `ldapb`, `ldaph`, `ldapw`, `ldapd`, `ldapq`, `stapb`, `staph`, `stapw`, `stapd`, `stapq` | 1–8 | 0,2,3,5 | Loads/stores through a protected-mode array pointer plus an index, checked against its bounds (SIGSEGV `SEGV_BNDERR`): every pointer access of lcc's protected code (`-mptr128`); SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPN` in a 64-bit process. (spec/abi/protected-mode.md) |  |  | semc (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `ldrd`, `strd` | 1–8 | 0,2,3,5 | Privileged register-space access; SIGILL `ILL_PRVOPC` in user mode. |  |  | semc (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `ldodpb`, `ldodph`, `ldodpw`, `ldodpd`, `ldodpq`, `ldodrb`, … (30 operations) | 1–2 | 0,2,3,5 | Object-descriptor accesses of v2's protected mode, gone from v3: `stodwd` is SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC` on the 4C, while `ldodwd`'s encoding (and `stodwd`'s on the 8C2) runs without a fault, as some later operation (`v2ops.c`). |  |  | v2ops (4C, 8C2, 2C3); 2 of 30 |

## Array prefetch and AAU registers

The array prefetch unit runs a program prepared by `ldisp %ctpr2` and started by `bap`; `mova*` read its buffer in channels 0–3 (apb.md, which gives the correctness rules).

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `movab`, `movah`, `movaw`, `movad`, `movaq`, `movaqp` | 1–7 |  | Read the next element(s) of an array prefetch area: base + index + displacement + step × n, zero-extended; a diagnostic value instead of a fault. 5 cycles. `movaqp` is v5+: gas accepts it for v3, where it writes a diagnostic value. **Use:** Software-pipelined loops in `loop_mode` (lcc at -O2+). (apb.md) |  | 11k / 10k | apb-loop, apb-stream, apb, apbleft… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `bap`, `eap`, `fapb` | 1–7 |  | `bap` starts the prefetch program, `eap` stops it; `fapb` is the program's own instruction format (written by `ldisp` targets). (apb.md) |  | 4.1k / 4.0k | apb-loop, apb-stream, apb, apbleft… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `aaurr`, `aaurrd`, `aaurrq`, `aaurw`, `aaurwd`, `aaurwq` | 1–8 | 2,5 | Read or write AAU registers (`%aadN`, `%aaindN`, `%aaincrN`, `%aastiN`, `%aabfN`, …); `aaurr*` of positions read 0 in user mode, `aaurrq` of a descriptor reads it back. ALC2/5. **Use:** Loop setup for `staa`/`ldaa`/APB. (apb.md, "AAU registers") |  | 29k / 30k | aaurwct, apb-loop, apb-stream, apb… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `incr` | 1–7 |  | Advance an AAU store/load index (`%aastiN += %aaincrN × size`), in the CDS syllable. (apb.md) |  | 696 / 883 | apbleft, apbst, loops, memleft… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

## Tags, protected mode and pointers

Registers carry tags (diagnostic values, protected-mode pointers). Ordinary C code meets tags only through speculation (speculation.md); these operations matter to protected mode.

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gettags`, `gettagd`, `puttags`, `puttagd` | 1–8 | 2,5 | `gettag*`: the tags of a (`gettagd` both halves, 0–15; `gettags` the low half's, 0–3) as a 32-bit result; no trap on a diagnostic a. `puttag*`: a with tags b (its low 4 bits; `puttags` 2); SIGILL `ILL_PRVOPC` when asked for a diagnostic half (tag 1 with bit 30 set) or a pointer tag (2, 3) not next to an empty half (`puttags`: any 2 or 3); `,sm` gives a diagnostic value (bit 30 set) instead. `puttag* a, 0` clears without checking a; a diagnostic b is `ILL_ILLOPN`. **Use:** Clearing the tag of a speculatively loaded word (lcc's `ld_*_cleartag` builtins; lcc always uses tag 0). (semantics.md, "Tag operations"; speculation.md, "Diagnostic values", "What lcc speculates") | 1; a 64-bit reader of a `gettag*` or `puttags` result waits 4 under `dbl = 0` (timing.md, Formats) | 2.4k / 2.2k | abg, abi/ctxsig.s, abi/foldi55, abi/foldp129_greg… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `movts`, `movtd`, `movtq` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | Copy keeping tags (`movtq` every tag, `movtd` turns a tag-3 half into 0, `movts` keeps only tag 1: semantics.md, "Tag operations"); `movtd a, %ctprN` prepares a transfer to the address in a (9 cycles to `ct`; ALC0). Under a predicate, `movtd` into a CTPR is SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC` whether the predicate is true or false (gas accepts it; MCST's qemu runs it conditionally: predicates.md, "RLP"). **Use:** Indirect calls and jumps (`movtd` + `ct`/`call`). (control-transfer.md) | 2; 9 (`movtd` to `ct`) | 7.6k / 7.4k | abg, abi/callsstack_tail.s, abi/ctpr.s, abi/ctxsig.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `movtcs`, `movtcd`, `movtcq`, `movtrs`, `movtrd`, `movtrq`, `movtrcs`, `movtrcd`, `movtrcq` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | Tag-converting moves; plain copies of untagged values. |  |  | semc (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `gettc`, `gettst`, `invtc`, `puttc`, `puttst` | 1–8 | 0,3 | Tag/trap-cell state: `gettc`, `puttc`, `puttst` SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC` in user mode, `gettst` leaves its destination, `invtc` returns an undecoded value. |  |  | semc (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `getpl` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | Prepare a transfer to the offset a from the compilation unit's start (`getpl a, %ctprN`, ALC0) (guide 10.9.2). Into a register: SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPN` with semc's operand in a 64-bit process; in a 32-bit or protected process a procedure label (v3–v5: the address with tag 0xA; v6: a 128-bit label in an even pair with the module's index in the high word, an odd destination SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC`). **Use:** lcc's indirect calls in 32-bit mode (`-mptr32`), 9 cycles before the `call`; function addresses in protected mode (`-mptr128`). (control-transfer.md; spec/abi/mode32.md, "Timing"; spec/abi/protected-mode.md) | 9 to `ct` or `call`, as `movtd` |  | abi/mode32/lat32, abi/mode32/mode32.s, semc (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `aptoap`, `aptoapb`, `cudtoap`, `gdtoap`, `getsap`, `getva`, `vfsi` | 1–8 | 0,1,3,4 | Protected-mode pointer conversions and checks (v2–v6). In ordinary user mode `aptoap`, `aptoapb` are SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPN`, `cudtoap`, `gdtoap` SIGSEGV `SEGV_BNDERR`, `getsap` SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC`, `vfsi` SIGBUS `BUS_ADRALN`; `getva a, b` returns the low 48 bits of the pointer a plus b (a = (0x0123456789abcdef, 0x10), b = 0x10 gives 0x456789abcdff). In a protected process (`-mptr128`) they make and narrow pointers: `getsap` allocates stack, `aptoap`/`aptoapb` narrow, `gdtoap` points into the globals, `cudtoap` gives a read-only AP to the module's code (lcc never emits it), `getva` gives an address. (spec/abi/protected-mode.md, "Operations") |  |  | abi/protected/pmmin.s, semc (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `cast`, `odtoap`, `tdtomp`, `gettd`, `getsod` | 1–2 | 0,1,3,4 | Object-descriptor operations of v2's protected mode; SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC` on v3 and v5 (`v2ops.c`). |  |  | v2ops (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

## Registers and state

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rrs`, `rrd`, `rws`, `rwd` | 1–8 | 0 | Read or write a state register: in user mode `%pfpfr`, `%fpcr`, `%fpsr` (FP control and status), `%lsr`/`%ilcr` (loops), `%clkr` (cycle counter), `%ip`, `%idr`, `%core_mode`, `%dimar0/1`, the stack registers (`%usd`, `%psp`, `%pshtp`, `%pcsp`, `%pcshtp`, `%sbr`, `%wd`, `%br`, `%cr0`, `%cr1`: reads checked, writes not tried; MCST's qemu stops on `%psp`, `%pshtp`, `%sbr`, `%br`), …; ALC0, one a cycle. `rrs` gives the low 32 bits (under `dbl = 0` the destination's upper half is kept, under `dbl = 1` zeroed, but the 4C then writes all 64 bits of `%clkr` and `%ip`); `rrd` zero-extends a 32-bit register (registers.md, `dbl`). `rwd %lsr` needs 4 cycles before `rrd %lsr` or the loop and 5 before `rrd %ilcr` (v5 `%lsr1` the same; loops.md, "Registers"); a write of the FP state is seen by the next operation but does not overlap a divide in flight (timing.md, "Every v3 operation"). **Use:** `fenv`, the GOT base (`rrd %ip`), loop counts, cycle counting. (registers.yaml; spec/abi/registers.md; spec/abi/stack-and-unwinding.md, "Stack registers") | 2 (`%ip`, `%upsr`, `%clkr`, `%idr`); 4 (`%core_mode`); 11 (`%pfpfr`, `%fpcr`, `%fpsr`) | 18k / 24k | aaurwct, abg, abi/abileft.s, abi/ctxsig.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `getsp` | 1–8 | 0 | Allocate (negative b) or release stack in the user stack and return the new stack pointer, the sum rounded down to 16 bytes; `getsp 0` reads it. 2 cycles. The amount must be a window register or `%g16`+. One past the part of the stack `USD` covers traps, and the kernel grows the stack by the amount rounded up to a page, at least 16 KiB. It touches no memory, so it is no stack probe; a release is not bounded by the frame; under a predicate it runs only when true. **Use:** `allocate_stack`, frame setup; a positive amount frees a VLA or, before a sibling call's `ct`, the whole frame (spec/abi/calling-convention.md, "Tail calls that release the frame"). (spec/abi/stack-and-unwinding.md, "User stack"; spec/abi/kernel-interface.md, "The data stack") | 2 | 10k / 10k | aaurwct, abi/callsstack_clash.s, abi/callsstack_tail.s, abi/ctxsig.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

## Predicates

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pass`, `andp`, `landp`, `movep` | 1–7 |  | PLS logic on primary predicates `@pN`: `pass` loads a `%pred` or a special predicate (`%lcntex`, `%spred`, `%rndpred`) into `@p0`-`@p3`, or writes a CLP result back to a `%pred`; `andp`/`landp` give c0 && c1 (each optionally negated; `landp`'s second operand is lazy for diagnostic values); `movep c, v` writes v to its `%pred` only when c is true. 1 cycle through a `%pred`, 0 within a wide instruction (two levels at most). **Use:** Branch conditions, if-conversion of `&&`/`\|\|` chains (lcc does every conjunction with `landp`, and uses `andp` only to copy or invert). (predicates.md; semantics.md, "Predicate logic"; bundle.md, "PLS") | 1; 0 within an instruction | 603k / 601k | abi/ctxsig.s, ctl6, ctlleft, ctlops… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `clpandp`, `clplandp` | 1–7 |  | Stand-alone predicate logic outside a wide instruction, `clpandp %predA, %predB, %predC` (gas expands it into PLS syllables); runs in user mode. |  |  | ctlops (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `srp`, `crp`, `slrp` | 1–7 |  | SS bits that set (`srp`), clear (`crp`) or set a loop (`slrp`) recovery point for the x86 binary translator, with an optional condition `? %predN` (binutils `parse_srp_args`): `srp`/`slrp` write their own address and BR to `%rpr` and start generations mode, `crp` ends it. Not used by lcc. In user mode they run on every machine, but in generations mode a lock-wait load is SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC` on v3/v5, and on v6 a lock-wait load, a fault or an instruction-cache fill raises the recovery-point exception (SIGBUS `BUS_OBJERR`), most likely what ctlops.c's earlier SIGILL (8C2) and SIGBUS (2C3) were. (speculation.md, "Recovery points") |  |  | ctlops, native, rp (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `set_mark`, `vfdi` | 1–7 |  | SS bits (`set_mark` the `sw` bit, `vfdi` a verify bit); both run in user mode without visible effect. The instruction monitor's `HS_SW` event (DIM0 0x0f) counts executed instructions with the `sw` bit, so `set_mark` marks instructions to count (pmu2.c `sw_mark`, 4C, 8C2, 2C3); `vfdi`'s meaning is not documented. (monitors.md, "Pipeline repeats and the rest"; bundle.md, "HS") |  |  | ctlops, pmu2 (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |

## Control transfer

A transfer is prepared into `%ctpr1–3` (`disp`, `return`, `movtd`, `getpl`, `sdisp`), then executed by `ct`, `call` or a condition on it; `ibranch` needs no preparation but costs 6 cycles when taken (control-transfer.md).

| Operations | ISA | ALC | Does | Lat | lcc v3 / v5 | Run on hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `disp`, `ldisp`, `sdisp`, `return`, `gettsd` | 1–7 |  | Prepare a `%ctpr`: `disp` a label (5 cycles to `ct`), `ldisp` an array prefetch program (`%ctpr2`), `sdisp %ctprN, NUM` a system call entry (glibc: `sdisp %ctpr1, 3` + `call`; 1 for 32-bit, 8 for protected mode), `return` the caller (6 cycles); `gettsd %ctprN` (v3+) runs in user mode. **Use:** Branches, calls (`disp` + `call`), returns, system calls (`sdisp` + `call`). (control-transfer.md) | 5 (`disp`), 6 (`return`) to `ct` | 233k / 229k | aaurwct, abg, abi/abileft.s, abi/callsstack_clash.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `ct`, `call`, `ibranch`, `rbranch` | 1–7 |  | `ct %ctprN ? cond` transfers (free when prepared in time); `call %ctprN, wbs = N` calls with a new window; `ibranch` is a direct branch (taken: 6 cycles); `rbranch` returns into a recovery block on `%MLOCK` or `%dt_alN`. **Use:** `jump`, `cbranch`, `call`, `return`, check-recovery. (control-transfer.md, speculation.md) |  | 263k / 259k | aaurwct, abg, abi/abileft.s, abi/callsstack_clash.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `pref` | 1–7 |  | Prefetch code at a label into the instruction cache, `pref %iprN, label` (guide 10.9.6); runs in user mode. It starts fetching at once, like an early `disp` without a CTPR, and given about 20 cycles' lead (code in L2) or 200–255 (code in memory) hides the miss, also before an `ibranch` and across a call; it fetches about as deep as `ipd 2` (`ctlleft.c`, 4C, 8C2, 2C3). **Use:** Cold code reached through a call or an `ibranch`, a few hundred cycles ahead; only with a global symbol (gas relocates a local label wrongly: elf.md, `R_E2K_PREF`). lcc doesn't emit it. (control-transfer.md, "Code not in the instruction cache") |  |  | ctlleft, ctlops (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `ipd`, `nop`, `wait` | 1–7 |  | `ipd N` instruction prefetch depth of a preparation (0–3; it matters only for code not in the instruction cache: control-transfer.md); `nop N` N empty cycles after the instruction; `wait` orders memory (`ld_c`, `st_c`, …: atomics.md, fences; the v5+ and v6+ fields: bundle.md, CS1): 6–7 cycles with nothing outstanding; a store and then the `wait` take 15–16 cycles with `st_c`, 20–33 with `ma_c`, and 6–7 with a v5+ soft modifier, which also cuts the `wait` alone to 2 (timing.md, "Every v3 operation"); `wait trap = 1` never returns in user mode. **Use:** `ipd` as lcc; `wait st_c` for C11 seq_cst stores; `nop` for delays under `.ignore strict_delay`. |  | 733k / 508k | aaurwct, abg, abi/callsstack_clash.s, abi/callsstack_tail.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `setwd`, `setbn`, `setbp`, `vfrpsz` | 1–7 |  | `setwd` sets the window size, `nfx` and `dbl`; `setbn`/`setbp` the rotating register and predicate areas. A `setwd wsz` smaller than the parameter area the caller handed over (the caller's wsz − its `call`'s wbs, in pairs) is SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC`. `vfrpsz rpsz = N` checks that area: more than N pairs is SIGSEGV `SEGV_BNDERR` (the window-bounds exception), N or fewer runs, in the function's first instruction or its second (the only ones tried; `ctlleft.c` `vfrpsz`: N 0–8, 12, 16, 31 against 0–8 and 12 pairs; 4C, 8C2, 2C3). gas encodes `vfrpsz` only together with a `setwd` (CS1 opcode 1) and writes `wsz = 0` when none is given, so a lone `vfrpsz` in a function that was handed anything gets the window check's SIGILL (the earlier `ctlops.c` result); when both checks fail only the SIGILL is seen. **Use:** `vfrpsz`: the kernel's entries only (`rpsz = 4`, protected mode 8; kernel `trap_table.S`); a compiler has no use for it. (spec/abi/registers.md; loops.md; spec/abi/kernel-interface.md, "System calls") |  | 72k / 72k | aaurwct, abg, abi/abileft.s, abi/callsstack_clash.s… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `loop_mode`, `alc`, `abn`, `abp`, `abg` | 1–7 |  | Loop mode and counters: `loop_mode` marks the loop, `alc` advances the loop counters, `abn`/`abp` rotate the register and predicate areas, `abg` the global registers (`%bgr`). (loops.md) |  | 51k / 50k | abg, abi/debuginfo.s, apb-loop, apb-stream… (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `flushr`, `flushc`, `flushts` | 1–7 |  | Spill the register window stack (`flushr`) or the chain stack (`flushc`) to memory; `flushts` flushes the trap stack. `flushr`, `flushc`, `flushts` run in user mode. **Use:** Stack walking (unwinders, `setjmp`-style code) needs the stacks in memory. |  |  | ctl6, ctlleft, ctlops (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `setsft` | 2–7 |  | Software trap: SIGTRAP `TRAP_BRKPT` in user mode (the kernel's `BUG()` uses it). **Use:** `trap` (`__builtin_trap`) as a breakpoint-style trap; lcc stores to address 0 instead. |  |  | ctlops (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `settr`, `setei` | 1–7 |  | System settings: `settr type = N` is SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC` in user mode, `setei` runs without visible effect. |  |  | ctlops (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `done` | 1–7 |  | Privileged return from a trap handler: SIGILL `ILL_PRVOPC` in user mode. |  |  | ctlops (4C, 8C2, 2C3) |
| `mmurr`, `mmurw` | 1–7 |  | MMU register access, privileged except `mmurw x, %dam_inv`, which clears the data speculation table (lcc writes it at the exits of loops with check loads); `mmurr` of the monitor registers is SIGILL. (speculation.md; monitors.md) |  |  | pmu, spec (4C, 8C2, 2C3); 1 of 2 |
